hints.title: Digit Permutation Next Greater Step
hints.text: The problem is equivalent to finding the next lexicographical permutation of the decimal digits of integer n.

hints.title: Pivot Scan and Suffix Reversal
hints.text: Scan right-to-left for the first decreasing digit. Swap it with the smallest larger digit to its right, then reverse the descending suffix.

hints.title: Signed 32-Bit Integer Bound Verification
hints.text: Convert the mutated digit list back to an integer. If no next permutation exists or if the resulting integer exceeds 2^31 - 1, return minus 1.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def nextGreaterElement(self, n: int) -> int:
        digits = list(str(n))
        i = len(digits) - 2
        while i >= 0 and digits[i] >= digits[i + 1]:
            i -= 1
        if i < 0:
            return -1
        j = len(digits) - 1
        while digits[j] <= digits[i]:
            j -= 1
        digits[i], digits[j] = digits[j], digits[i]
        digits[i + 1:] = reversed(digits[i + 1:])
        val = int("".join(digits))
        return val if val <= 2**31 - 1 else -1
```

variables: N: value of n (at most 10 decimal digits)
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(log N) time and O(log N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Iterating through n + 1, n + 2, ... testing digit multiset equality is far too slow and times out.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Next-permutation algorithm runs on the 10-digit array in linear digit time with tiny temporary array space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should check the 32-bit signed integer overflow upper bound 2147483647.
